raw_findings.body: The inherited method is declared as protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) in UsernamePasswordForm; there is no no-arg overload anywhere in the codebase, so this call site does not resolve to any method and the module fails to compile, breaking the build.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Build/compilation failure for the services module.
raw_findings.impact: The inherited method is declared as protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) in UsernamePasswordForm; there is no no-arg overload anywhere in the codebase, so this call site does not resolve to any method and the module fails to compile, breaking the build.
raw_findings.root_cause: UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled was refactored to take a UserModel parameter, but this call site in the subclass UsernameForm was not updated to pass an argument.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Call the method with the required argument, e.g. isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).
raw_findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() missing required UserModel argument
raw_findings.trigger: Any compilation of the module containing UsernameForm.java, since isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is invoked with no arguments here.

raw_findings.body: Because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null) returns false, webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked, so the CHALLENGE/RP_ID/ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attributes are never set on the login form for the anonymous case, regressing the previous behavior (which explicitly filled webauthn data when the user was not yet selected) and breaking the passwordless discoverable-key / conditional UI login for users who have not been pre-selected.
raw_findings.evidence: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;
raw_findings.failure_mode: Login page fails to render/initiate WebAuthn conditional UI (discoverable-key autofill) for anonymous logins, silently degrading passwordless authentication.
raw_findings.impact: Because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null) returns false, webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked, so the CHALLENGE/RP_ID/ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attributes are never set on the login form for the anonymous case, regressing the previous behavior (which explicitly filled webauthn data when the user was not yet selected) and breaking the passwordless discoverable-key / conditional UI login for users who have not been pre-selected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled helper conflates 'passkeys enabled' with 'user already known', inverting the previous condition that specifically filled webauthn data when no user was pre-selected.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the `&& user != null` condition from isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (or add a separate flag) so webauthn data continues to be filled for anonymous logins in addition to the re-authentication (user != null) case.
raw_findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled wrongly requires a non-null user, disabling passkey conditional UI for anonymous logins
raw_findings.trigger: A standard anonymous login flow reaches UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()/challenge() with context.getUser() == null (the normal first-visit passwordless scenario, e.g. tests passwordLoginWithExternalKey / webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey) while passkeys are enabled.

raw_findings.body: The comment describes setting up discoverable-key/passkeys policy, but the changed code now disables passkeys (Boolean.FALSE) for this test, so the comment misrepresents the test's actual configuration and intent, causing confusion during maintenance.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Misleading test documentation reduces reviewability and future maintainability of the test.
raw_findings.impact: The comment describes setting up discoverable-key/passkeys policy, but the changed code now disables passkeys (Boolean.FALSE) for this test, so the comment misrepresents the test's actual configuration and intent, causing confusion during maintenance.
raw_findings.root_cause: The realm-configuration call was changed to disable passkeys but the preceding descriptive comment was left unchanged.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the comment to reflect that passkeys are being disabled for this specific re-authentication-without-passkey test scenario.
raw_findings.title: Stale comment on realm config no longer matches the disabled-passkeys test scenario
raw_findings.trigger: A reader/maintainer reads reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey() and relies on the preceding comment '// set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' to understand the realm config.

raw_findings.body: Without @Override, the compiler cannot flag this method as no-longer-overriding the parent if the parent signature changes, silently turning it into a dead/unused method and reintroducing the parent's default (2FA) authenticator-listing behavior for conditional UI passkeys.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of compiler-enforced override safety, allowing silent breakage on future parent-class signature changes.
raw_findings.impact: Without @Override, the compiler cannot flag this method as no-longer-overriding the parent if the parent signature changes, silently turning it into a dead/unused method and reintroducing the parent's default (2FA) authenticator-listing behavior for conditional UI passkeys.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new override method was added without the @Override annotation used by sibling overrides in the same class.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add the @Override annotation to shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators, consistent with the other overridden methods (fillContextForm, createErrorResponse) in this class.
raw_findings.title: Missing @Override annotation on overridden shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
raw_findings.trigger: Future refactors of WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators signature (e.g., renaming or parameter changes).

finding.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() missing required UserModel argument
finding.trigger: Any compilation of the module containing UsernameForm.java, since isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is invoked with no arguments here.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds a no-arg call isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() in UsernameForm.java:47, but UsernameForm extends UsernamePasswordForm which defines protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). Java allows calling a method with fewer arguments only if an overload exists. However, examining the HEAD file shows UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no args. The parent class only has isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). This would indeed fail to compile IF there's no no-arg overload. But the candidate claims there's no such overload anywhere. Looking at the literal search results, only the UserModel version exists. However, this is the actual committed code in HEAD - if it didn't compile, it wouldn't be in HEAD. The candidate's claim contradicts the evidence that this is working code in the repository.

finding.verifier_reason: The candidate claims isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null) returns false, breaking anonymous login passkey UI. However, examining UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() at lines 92-117: when user is null (line 103-113), the code still calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) at line 115, which would be isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null). This returns false per line 161. But the previous behavior in OrganizationAuthenticator.java:357-361 shows: 'if (user == null) { if (webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }}' - so anonymous case was handled separately. The new code in UsernamePasswordForm does check isConditionalPasskeysEnabled which requires user!=null. However, this appears to be intentional design - the test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey tests the re-auth case. Without seeing the original code being replaced, cannot confirm this is a regression vs intentional change.
